writeup.headline: LyondellBasell rates Hold: a sharp quarterly revenue rebound offsets thin margins and a stretched balance sheet.
writeup.thesis: LyondellBasell scores 50, a Hold, sitting 6 points above the Sell line and 15 points below Buy. Growth is the strongest factor at 65, driven by latest-quarter revenue growth of 19.8% year on year, with growth that sped up by 26.1 pp from the previous quarter, though the longer view still shows a TTM revenue decline of 1.8%. Quality (37) and balance sheet (26) hold the score back: the operating margin is 3.1%, the FCF margin is 5.1%, net debt is 5.61 times free cash flow and cash covers only 0.31 of debt. Valuation scores 58: in absolute terms P/S of 0.7x is low and the FCF yield is 2.3 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield, but EV/EBIT of 31.7x is high, and overall the multiples sit near the middle of its own history, with P/FCF more expensive than at 43 of the last 61 month-ends. Trend (58) is mixed, with the price 7.0% above its 50-day average but shares 15.6 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, and news risk (46) reflects mostly negative analyst moves.
key_risks: Leverage: net debt at 5.61 times free cash flow and cash covering 0.31 of debt leave little room if cash flow weakens.
Thin margins (3.1% operating, 12.8% gross) make earnings sensitive to weak chemical demand and pricing.
Analyst sentiment has turned cautious, including a Citi downgrade to Neutral and BofA keeping Underperform.
Q3 results due 2026-10-30 could undercut the recent revenue rebound, especially with Middle East-related volatility.
EV/EBIT of 31.7x is high in absolute terms and more expensive than at 47 of the last 61 month-ends.
what_would_change: A drop of 6 points would push the rating to Sell, for example if Q3 results reverse the quarterly growth acceleration or analyst actions worsen further.
A move to Buy needs 15 more points, likely requiring better quality scores through higher margins alongside sustained revenue growth.
Delivering the $500 million Cash Improvement Plan target and reducing net debt would lift the weak balance sheet score.
A recovery in relative performance against SPY and QQQ would strengthen the trend factor.
